---
applyTo: "charts/stable/**,charts/incubator/**"
description: "Rules for TrueCharts application charts (charts/stable and charts/incubator)"

# Application chart instructions

These rules apply to application charts in `charts/stable/<chart>/` and `charts/incubator/<chart>/`. They add to the general rules in [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md): minimal changes, a SemVer bump of `version` on every non-docs change, and no edits to generated files.

## Chart layout

```text
charts/stable/<chart>/
├── Chart.yaml            # bump `version` for every non-docs change
├── values.yaml           # chart configuration; only overrides of `common` defaults
├── templates/
│   ├── common.yaml       # {{ include "tc.v1.common.loader.all" . }}
│   ├── NOTES.txt         # {{- include "tc.v1.common.lib.chart.notes" $ -}}
│   └── _<name>.tpl       # optional, chart-specific helpers only
├── ci/*-values.yaml      # optional, install-test values (CI runs one install per file)
├── docs/*.md             # optional, user docs (frontmatter `title:`); no version bump needed
├── README.md             # GENERATED: do not edit
├── CHANGELOG.md          # GENERATED: do not edit
├── .helmignore           # GENERATED: do not edit
└── icon.webp, icon-small.webp  # GENERATED by the daily workflow from an icon.<ext> (e.g. icon.png)
```

Charts are thin wrappers around the `common` library. Express everything through values that `common` understands, such as `workload`, `service`, `persistence`, `configmap`, `secret`, `ingress`, `cnpg`, `metrics` and `addons`. Do not hand-write Kubernetes manifests in `templates/`. The library documentation is at <https://trueforge.org/truecharts-common>, with the sources in `charts/library/common/docs/`.

`charts/stable/app-template` is the minimal reference chart; copy its structure when creating a new chart.

## `Chart.yaml`

- Bump `version` following the SemVer table in `AGENTS.md`:
  - **major**: breaking changes (renamed or removed keys, changed ports or persistence paths, major app upgrade, migration needed)
  - **minor**: features and minor app upgrades
  - **patch**: fixes, patch app upgrades and digest changes
- Dependencies:
  - `common` must be the **first** dependency, from `oci://oci.trueforge.org/truecharts`.
  - Other TrueCharts dependencies (e.g. `valkey` with `alias: redis` and `condition: redis.enabled`; `mariadb`; `mongodb`) come from the same OCI repository and are listed alphabetically after `common`.
  - Keep the full dependency block format used by existing charts (`condition`, `alias`, `tags` and `import-values` keys present).
  - Never use `file://` dependencies in app charts.
  - Do not bump the `common` version by hand unless the task requires a feature from a newer `common`. Renovate handles routine bumps.
- Don't edit the fields that `forgetool` manages, as listed in `AGENTS.md`: helm/kube annotations, `kubeVersion`, `maintainers`, `home`, `icon`, `sources` and `appVersion`.
- Adding a new chart: set the `description`, `keywords`, `type: application`, `version` and a `trueforge.org/category` annotation. Copy the remaining fields from an existing chart, and add an `icon.png` (or other `icon.<ext>`) for the daily workflow to convert.

## `values.yaml`

- Keep the first line exactly: `# yaml-language-server: $schema=./values.schema.json`.
- Only set values that differ from the `common` defaults in `charts/library/common/values.yaml`. Do not copy defaults.
- Images:
  - Use `image: { repository, pullPolicy: IfNotPresent, tag: <version>@sha256:<digest> }`. Always pin by digest; Renovate keeps both the tag and the digest up to date.
  - Put extra images in `<name>Image` keys (e.g. `postgresImage`, `configImage`) and select them in containers with `imageSelector: <name>Image`.
- The primary workload, container, service and port are named `main`. Keep existing object names, ports, keys and persistence `mountPath`s stable, because renaming them breaks upgrades and needs a **major** bump.
- Security:
  - `common` defaults to UID/GID `568`, `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, no privilege escalation and dropped capabilities.
  - Only relax these (e.g. `runAsNonRoot: false`, `runAsUser: 0`, `readOnlyRootFilesystem: false`) when the app actually requires it, and leave a short comment explaining why.
- Persistence: all user data and configuration must be stored on `persistence` volumes and survive restarts and upgrades.
- Databases and caches:
  - Use the built-in helpers rather than custom deployments.
  - PostgreSQL: `cnpg.main` (set `enabled`, `user` and `database`). Reference credentials via `.Values.cnpg.main.creds.*` in `tpl` strings, or via `secretKeyRef` to `cnpg-main-urls` (keys such as `host`, `std`, `jdbc`).
  - Valkey/Redis: the `redis` dependency, using `.Values.redis.creds.*`.
  - MariaDB and MongoDB: the `mariadb` and `mongodb` dependencies.
- Most `common` value strings are rendered with `tpl` (see the "Helm `tpl`" row in the common docs), so you can reference other values, e.g. `"{{ .Values.service.main.ports.main.port }}"`.
- App requirements, from the TrueCharts development guidelines:
  - no default or hard-coded passwords: generate secrets in templates, or let `common`/the dependencies generate them
  - no manual config-file editing required to get a working app
  - sensible, secure defaults

## Custom templates

Only add templates when values alone are not enough. Follow the existing pattern (see `charts/stable/anonaddy`):

```yaml
{{/* templates/common.yaml */}}
{{- include "tc.v1.common.loader.init" . -}}

{{- $secrets := include "<chart>.secrets" . | fromYaml -}}
{{- if $secrets -}}
  {{- $_ := set .Values.secret "<chart>-secrets" $secrets -}}
{{- end -}}

{{- include "tc.v1.common.loader.apply" . -}}
```

- Define helpers in `templates/_<name>.tpl`, named `<chart>.<name>`.
- Generated secrets must stay stable across upgrades. Look up the existing Secret with `lookup` and reuse its data, falling back to `randAlphaNum` only on first install.

## Tests (`ci/`)

- CI installs each changed chart in a k3d cluster with `ct install`. It runs once per `ci/*-values.yaml` file, or with the default values if there are none. If a chart has a `test-chart/` subdirectory, CI installs that wrapper chart instead.
- Add or update a `ci/*-values.yaml` file when a change can't be exercised with the defaults (e.g. optional features, alternative databases).
- Charts that cannot run in CI (game servers, hardware-dependent apps, etc.) are listed in `.github/ct-install.yaml` `excluded-charts`. Do not add charts there just to make CI pass.

## Docs

- User-facing docs go in `charts/<train>/<chart>/docs/*.md`. Each file needs frontmatter with a `title:`.
- Changes that only touch `docs/` do not need a version bump.

## Validate locally

Run from the repository root, using the latest Helm 4 (see `AGENTS.md` → Toolchain):

```bash
chart=charts/stable/<chart>

helm dependency build "$chart"      # retry if oci.trueforge.org returns "unexpected EOF"
helm lint --strict "$chart"
helm template test "$chart" >/dev/null
for f in "$chart"/ci/*values.yaml; do [ -f "$f" ] && helm template test "$chart" -f "$f" >/dev/null; done

# CI lint: helm lint, Chart.yaml schema, yamllint and the version-bump check against master
git fetch origin master
result_file=/tmp/lint_result.txt .github/scripts/tc-lint.sh "[\"$chart\"]" origin/master

pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/master -- "$chart")

rm -rf "$chart/charts" "$chart/Chart.lock"   # never commit these
```

`tc-lint.sh` needs `helm`, `yamllint`, `yamale`, GNU `parallel` and `jq`.
